2026-12-16.title: Third Wednesday of Annunciation
2026-12-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Fidelity to the word of God
2026-12-16.verse: Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
theo: Paul thanks God that the Thessalonians received his preaching “not as a human word but as what it really is, God's word, which is also at work in you believers.” The word of God, received in faith, works in us.

Jesus teaches faithfulness in small things: honest dealings, trustworthy use of money, an undivided heart. “No slave can serve two masters… You cannot serve God and wealth.” As Christmas approaches, with its spending and celebrations, the Gospel asks whom we really serve.
outline: Ask: who is your master during the Christmas shopping season?
God's word received in faith transforms us.
God, not wealth, must rule our Christmas.
live: Spend less on yourself and give more to the poor this Christmas.
Read the Christmas Gospel (Luke 2:1–20) slowly this week.
2026-12-16.prayer: Lord, let your word work in me. Make me faithful in little things and free from the love of money, so that I serve you alone. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Word we hear becomes the Bread we receive. The word at work in us is nourished at the altar.

quick: God's word works in those who believe.
Faithful in little, faithful in much.
No one can serve God and wealth.
2026-12-16.action: Give more to the poor than to yourself this Christmas.
2026-12-16.question: Whom do I serve during this season?

family.explain: Jesus says if we are honest in small things, we will be honest in big things. We cannot love God and money both as masters.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always be honest.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can each of us do faithfully this week?”

pm.open: Lord, your word is at work in us who believe. As we gather, let us receive it not as a human word but as your own living word. Amen.
share: Paul says the word is at work in believers (1 Thessalonians 2:13). How has God's word worked in me this year?
Jesus speaks of faithfulness in very little (Luke 16:10). Where am I unfaithful in small things?
Am I serving God or wealth in my daily decisions?
pm.resp: Speak, Lord, your servants are listening.
interc: For the Church, that she may receive and proclaim God's word faithfully.
For those who suffer for their faithfulness to the Gospel.
For business people and workers, that they may be honest in all dealings.
For students, that they may be faithful in study and integrity.
For our prayer group, that God's word may bear fruit in us.
pm.close: Lord God, your word is living and active. Make us faithful in little things and in great, and let your word take flesh in our lives this Christmas. Amen.

illus: A shopkeeper in Ernakulam was offered a large order if he would write a false bill for the customer's company. He refused and lost the order. A year later the same customer came back: “I want a supplier I can trust.” Faithfulness in small things became much.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul thanks God that the Thessalonians received the word of God, which you heard from us, not as a human word but as what it really is, God's word, which is also at work in you believers (1 Thessalonians 2:13). The word of God is not only information; it is power at work in us.
How do we receive Scripture? As an old book? As a duty? Or as God speaking today? When we hear the readings in the Holy Qurbana with faith, the word works in us: consoling, correcting, calling.

The Thessalonians paid a price for receiving the word. They suffered from their own compatriots, as the churches in Judea had. Faithfulness to God's word sometimes costs us friends, opportunities or comfort.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of faithfulness in small things: whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much. No slave can serve two masters; you cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:10–13).

Faithfulness is tested in small daily matters: an honest bill, a promise kept, a prayer said even when tired, a tithe given, overtime not falsely claimed. These small things reveal whom we really serve.

This Nombu, let us read a small passage of the Gospel each day, receive it as God's own word, and ask: what does this mean for me today? And let us examine our faithfulness in little things. The God who comes at Christmas is faithful; let us be faithful to him. Amen.
kids: Children, being honest in small things makes Jesus very happy. Tell the truth even when it is hard!

intro: God's word at work; faithfulness in little; God, not wealth.

points.h: The word at work in you
sub: The Thessalonians received God's word as God's word.
q: If I say, “I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,” then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones.
Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.

sub: Christmas spending tests our honesty and generosity.
q: Honor the LORD with your substance and with the first fruits of all your produce.
If then you have not been faithful with the dishonest wealth, who will entrust to you the true riches?
points.apply: Give generously to the poor this Christmas.

sub: An undivided heart serves one master.
The Child in the manger chose poverty.
q: Hear, O Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone.
No slave can serve two masters; for a slave will either hate the one and love the other, or be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
points.apply: Spend less on yourself this Christmas.

concl: Let God's word rule our hearts this Christmas.
2026-12-16.resolve: Plan a simple, generous Christmas as a family.
